evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The is_in_or_equal function may be bypassed. Affected versions (<5.0) are vulnerable to Directory Traversal: an attacker can access restricted files by manipulating file paths using parent directory sequences. Ensure that all file paths are properly resolved and absolute. The CVE-2023-51449 fix in 4.11.0 (".." substring check) hardened the SAME is_in_or_equal containment guard but left abspath()'s symlink non-resolution in place; 5.0.0 adds .resolve().

provenance.notes: Real Docker verification with official PyPI gradio wheels (4.10.0/4.11.0/5.0.0) on python:3.11-slim, era-pinned web-stack deps. Same sink gradio.utils.is_in_or_equal (via the /file= route). Sink evolution (source-verified): V0 4.10.0 `str(rel).startswith('..')`; V1 4.11.0 `'..' in str(rel)` (CVE-2023-51449 fix); V2 5.0.0 `abspath(p).resolve()` (CVE-2024-47164 fix). ORIGINAL = /file=/gradio_tmp/sub/../../flag (subdir+.. escape) reads the canary on V0 (HTTP 200) and is blocked on V1 (HTTP 403). RESIDUAL = /file=/gradio_tmp/escape/flag (escape is a symlink -> / inside the allowed dir; abspath() never resolves symlinks, so the relative path has no '..') reads the canary on V1 (HTTP 200) and is closed on V2 (HTTP 403). V2 blocks both. Note: a pure literal-'..' residual is caught by V1's substring check, so the genuine V1-surviving residual is the symlink form that V2's added .resolve() closes; documented in _heldout/evidence.json. Gate run via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`; see repro.log.

audit.evidence: Live regate on real Docker (python:3.11-slim + UNMODIFIED pip gradio 4.10.0/4.11.0/5.0.0 running the real gradio server, minimal app.py). Gate passed via HTTP /file= route: original subdir/../.. containment escape flag@v0, blocked@v1 ('..' in rel), symlink-escape residual flag@v1 (abspath doesn't resolve symlink), both original+residual blocked@v2 (5.0.0 .resolve()). Real gradio package bytes => real-library-wrap.
